items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: I think Raymond Burke played a little bit. On the chameleon.

ctx.x: I think it was two side wheels. Raymond has pictures of it. He played on the boat.
I think Raymond Burke played a little bit. On the chameleon. It must have lasted pretty late then, didn't it?
No, it went out existing and it came back and it didn't stay very long.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-10-21
items.q: I believe Raymond Burke used to scrape the mouthpiece

ctx.x: I would like a wide layer. A wide layer, I could use a soft reed. A bind is bind with the mouthpiece. If you've got a close reed, you use a hard mouthpiece. Try to slide. Yeah, the layer you use a hard reed. If you've got a wide layer, use a soft reed.

I believe Raymond Burke used to scrape the mouthpiece, the layer of the mouthpiece on the ground to make it wider and that kind of thing. Did you ever do anything like that? No, no, no. I never tried.
I tried, in fact my daddy was living in a goat horn. I never heard a horn of a goat to make a reed and couldn't get nothing out of it.
